recipes.name: Korean Cheese Corn Dogs
ingredients: 1 large Russet potato, peeled and cut into one fourth inch cubes
For the Hot Dogs and Cheese
1 lb whole milk mozzarella, cut into hot dog sized sticks
1 cup Panko breadcrumbs, or as needed
instructions: For the Toppings
Begin by prepping the mozzarella and potatoes. - whole milk mozzarella cut into hot dog sized sticks - large Russet potato peeled and cut into one fourth inch cubes
Slice the mozzarella into hot-dog sized sticks. - 1 lb whole milk mozzarella cut into hot dog sized sticks
Cut the potatoes into small cubes. - 1 large Russet potato peeled and cut into one fourth inch cubes
Then, bring a medium pot of heavily salted water to a boil and add the potatoes, par-cooking for about 3-5 minutes. - large Russet potato peeled and cut into one fourth inch cubes
Meanwhile, prep a baking sheet lined with paper towels.
Transfer the potatoes to the prepped baking sheet to drain moisture and allow them to fully dry and cool. - 1 large Russet potato peeled and cut into one fourth inch cubes
Once the potatoes are dry and cool, toss in corn starch, using a fine mesh sieve to shake off the excess. - 2 tbsp cornstarch - 1 large Russet potato peeled and cut into one fourth inch cubes
Set aside.
For the Batter
While the potatoes are cooling, make the batter.
In a large rectangular container like a casserole dish, combine the flour and yeast. Whisk to fully combine. - 7 cups (910 g) flour - 2 tbsp instant yeast PLUS - 2 tsp instant yeast
Then, combine the water, sugar, and salt to a large spouted measuring cup and whisk well to fully dissolve the sugar and salt. - 4 cups lukewarm water - ½ cup sugar - 2 tsp kosher salt
Transfer the dry ingredients to a large mixing bowl, then add the water mixture and mix well with a wooden spoon. - For the Batter
Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for around an hour or so proofing. - For the Batter
For the Hot Dogs and Cheese
While the batter is proofing, assemble the hot dogs and cheese dogs.
Skewer a variety of hot dogs, mozzarella sticks, and half mozzarella-half hot dogs. - hot dogs - whole milk mozzarella cut into hot dog sized sticks
For the Assembly
Prepare wire cooling racks set inside baking sheets and layered with paper towels for draining.

Prepare dredging stations in the wide, shallow bowls. 1 with the Panko bread crumbs and 1 with potato cubes. - 1 cup Panko breadcrumbs or as needed - large Russet potato peeled and cut into one fourth inch cubes
Prepare a separate shallow bowl with granulated sugar. Set aside. - ½ cup sugar
Remove the batter from the fridge (it should be sticky and elastic) - For the Batter
Preheat a large, heavy bottomed pot with 5-6 inches of oil to 350°F. - vegetable oil for frying

Dip the skewered hot dogs, cheese-dogs, and hot-cheese dogs into the batter and use a twisting and pulling motion to evenly wrap it around the skewer. You may need to use your fingers to keep the dogs on the skewers. - For the Hot Dogs and Cheese - For the Batter
Then, coat each corn dog in a thick and even layer of Panko bread crumbs. - For the Hot Dogs and Cheese - 1 cup Panko breadcrumbs or as needed

Continue this battering process with each of the skewered hot dogs and mozzarella sticks, alternately coating with potato cubes and a layer of Panko bread crumbs, at your preference. - For the Batter - For the Hot Dogs and Cheese - 1 cup Panko breadcrumbs or as needed - For the Toppings
Fry each skewered dog in the preheated oil for about 2-3 minutes until everything is golden brown. - For the Hot Dogs and Cheese - vegetable oil for frying
Immediately after frying, set the corn dogs on the prepared baking sheets to drain. - For the Assembly
At your preference, roll the fried corn dogs in a light dusting of granulated sugar. - ½ cup sugar - For the Hot Dogs and Cheese
Serve hot with an optional drizzling of ketchup and mustard. - ketchup to taste - mustard to taste
